solutions.check: 28 of 30 entries, 50 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: What biology student must do makes moral sense

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a biology student has to con (study) science
the inner sense of right and wrong

explanation.surface: Studying biology somehow gives a student an ethical compass.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: to con is an old word for to study, so the student must con science.
explanation.definitionFit: The faculty that tells right from wrong is an inner moral sense, a synonym.

clue.text: Convict's first time in prison

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the word convict's is used

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A convict's first stretch behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage is a barred enclosure for confining, so loosely a prison.

clue.text: Young baby will have eaten no stew

indicators.note: to stew is to cook by stirring things together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: An infant will have been fed no stew yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the food the baby has not eaten, but it signals rearranging EATEN and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn infant in its first weeks is a neonate, the medical term.

clue.text: Guerrilla has a way of speaking to show disagreement

parts.note: the Contras were Nicaraguan guerrilla fighters of the 1980s
diction is one's manner of enunciating words

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter's manner of talking reveals dissent.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what someone states is opposition, a synonym for disagreement.

clue.text: Lavish old lover gets to write 'on diamonds

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to pen is to write
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A former partner splashes out on jewellery and writes about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lavish' is a verb here, meaning to spend freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish money is to spend it freely, so it is a synonym of spend out.

clue.text: Half of police involved with crime in a computing routine

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled together, so the letters are jumbled
half of says only the first three of the word's six letters are taken

explanation.surface: Some officers are mixed up in a computer crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges POL (half of police) with CRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A program that translates source code into machine code is a standard computing routine.

clue.text: Entrance men at party

indicators.note: at places the men beside the party, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a do is a party
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Men stationed at a party's entrance, like bouncers.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrance to a room or building is a doorway, its everyday synonym.

clue.text: Excessively superior to a colourless Canadian

indicators.note: in a down clue being superior means sitting above, so the first piece comes before the rest

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means excessively
wan means pale or colourless

explanation.surface: Someone excessively snooty towards a dull Canadian.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Canada's capital city is a Canadian, so a specific example.

clue.text: Where office workers may encounter growing overheads?

definitions.text: Where office workers may encounter growing overheads?

parts.words: Where office workers may encounter growing overheads?
parts.note: overheads sound like business costs, but it means plants growing above, on top of a building

explanation.surface: Office staff may face spiralling business costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted area on top of a building is literally greenery overhead, a cryptic description.

clue.text: Mature bunch seizing victory when one short

indicators.note: seizing means the outer word grabs and holds the other inside it

parts.note: a group is a bunch

indicators.note: one is the Roman numeral I, so the word loses that letter

parts.note: a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A mature team takes a victory despite being a player down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunch' reads as a cluster of flowers but is a team; the Roman numeral for one is what 'when one short' drops, leaving WN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mature is fully developed, an adult, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Wizard Communist leader has rest arrested and tortured

indicators.note: arrested means held in custody, so one piece is held within another

parts.note: Mao Zedong led Communist China

indicators.note: tortured means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Communist leader has someone detained and tortured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' suggests magic, but here it means a master; 'tortured' scrambles the rest to ESTR before it is locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard at something is a virtuoso or master, a synonym.

clue.text: One in white coat spotted the man responsible for language exam

definitions.meaning: a gundog breed with a white coat flecked with colour

definitions.text: the man responsible for language exam
definitions.meaning: whoever sets an exam in the English language

explanation.surface: Someone in a lab coat spotted the examiner behind a language test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'white coat' suggests a doctor or scientist, but it is a dog's fur.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a speckled white gundog, and a person who writes an English paper is literally its setter.

clue.text: Justifying a bishop having inadequate housing

indicators.note: housing means the outer word gives the other a home inside it

parts.note: wanting means falling short
RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop's poor accommodation is used to excuse something.
explanation.definitionFit: Justifying something is giving grounds that make it deserved, a synonym.

clue.text: Comedian has pay cut

indicators.note: cut means the word is docked at its tail

parts.note: a wage is pay

explanation.surface: A comic accepts a reduced fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A wag is a joker or wit, a synonym for a comedian.

clue.text: One old penny among two other bits of money in the same place

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

indicators.note: among places the pair of letters within the second unit of money

parts.note: a cent is a small unit of money
I is the Roman numeral one
D, from Latin denarius, was the abbreviation for a pre-1971 British penny

explanation.surface: A single old penny turns up among some other coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincident things occupy the same position or happen together, a synonym.

clue.text: Indian religious festival held by a number on return

indicators.note: held by puts the festival inside the reversed letters
on return means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival

explanation.surface: A Native American festival is marked by a number of people on their return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' means a Native American people, not someone from India; 'on return' gives ONA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oneida are a Native American people, so an example of an American Indian.

clue.text: One condescending to receive singular inventor

indicators.note: to receive means the outer word takes the letter in

parts.note: to deign is to condescend, so one who does is a deigner
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A patronising person welcomes an exceptional creator.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who devises new products or plans is a creator, close to an inventor.

clue.text: Pioneers developed a liquid for rubber manufacture

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Early innovators created a fluid used in making rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: This volatile hydrocarbon liquid is the building block of natural and synthetic rubber.

clue.text: Report of swans etc being set free

indicators.note: set free means let loose, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: News of swans and other birds being released.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast bulletin of the news is a report, so a synonym.

clue.text: Like some bread, only the first two slices of which may get consumed

indicators.note: the first two slices of means only the opening pair of letters of which is taken

parts.note: eaten means consumed

explanation.surface: A loaf of which only two slices may be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made from wheat flour is described as wheaten, an adjective for its grain.

clue.text: Control horse, except the tail

indicators.note: except the tail means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a charger is a cavalry horse

explanation.surface: Keep a horse in check apart from its swishing tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in charge is to have control, so as a noun the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Loner about to be given hint someone's beginning to interrupt

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: to interrupt means to break into, so the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a clue is a hint

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A hermit is about to be tipped off when someone starts butting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse lives withdrawn from society, so is a loner, a synonym.

clue.text: Sound honest to the listener

indicators.note: to the listener means the word is judged by how it is heard

parts.note: straight means honest

explanation.surface: Something sounds honest to whoever hears it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a verb but is the noun, a narrow sea channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of water between two land masses, a geographical synonym.

clue.text: Insects: bumping fifty off takes such an age

indicators.note: bumping off means killing, so the letter is removed

parts.note: lice are insects
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Killing off fifty insects takes ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bumping off' together signal removing L; 'such an age' is the Ice Age.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ice Age was a long glacial period, so the word fits as the kind of age.

clue.text: Irritability? Arrange a nice time to keep quiet

indicators.note: to keep means the scrambled letters hold the other one inside
arrange means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P, piano, is the music abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: Getting irritated, someone wants to arrange a pleasant time to keep things quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' rearranges A NICE TIME into IMATIENCE, which keeps P inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short-tempered and unable to wait is irritability, a near synonym.

clue.text: Access has deteriorated beyond repair with roof gone

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: had it means worn out beyond fixing

explanation.surface: An entrance has crumbled past saving now that the roof is lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with roof gone' drops H from HADIT. An adit is a horizontal mine entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal passage giving access to a mine, a synonym.

clue.text: Not all dissident entertainers will get international understanding

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every dissident performer will get on with foreign audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'will get', which is a link joining wordplay to definition; the defining words are 'international understanding'.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, so an international understanding.

clue.text: A report coming around beginning of term would be surprise

indicators.note: coming around means the outer word goes round the other

parts.note: a report is a loud noise, a sound

indicators.note: beginning of means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A rumour going round at the start of term would come as a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound someone is to surprise them greatly, a stronger synonym.

clue.text: Time to go to old American city for award there

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: Time to head to an old American city to collect a prize there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' refers back to America: the Tony is the Broadway theatre award.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre's prize in the United States is the Tony, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: Reform of gambler, this person having encountered Scripture

parts.note: a better is one who bets
this person refers to the speaker, me
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A reformed gambler who has found religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Reform means improvement, and betterment is a synonym for improvement.
